title: Redox Reactions
standard_text: Oxidation as a loss of electrons and reduction as a gain of electrons; oxidation numbers; oxidising and reducing agents; writing and balancing redox half-reactions and overall equations; the table of standard reduction potentials to predict reactions. (summary of the senior secondary Chemistry curriculum, SSS 2; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 Chemistry worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): oxidation and reduction, oxidation numbers, half-equations, redox reactions and half-reactions and reactivity and displacement. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: OIL RIG: oxidation is loss, reduction is gain of electrons.
body_html:
How to think about it

Oxidation is a loss of electrons (the oxidation number increases); reduction is a gain of electrons (the oxidation number decreases). Oxidation and reduction always happen together. Oxidation numbers: elements are 0, O is usually −2, H is usually +1, and they add up to the charge of the species.

The oxidising agent takes electrons and is itself reduced; the reducing agent gives electrons and is itself oxidised. Half-reactions show the electrons; the electrons lost must equal the electrons gained in the overall equation.

Example

Oxidation number of Mn in MnO₄⁻?

x + 4(−2) = −1

Answer: +7

Example

Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu. Which is oxidised?

Which loses electrons?

Answer: zinc

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the oxidising agent is oxidised.
  • Forgetting that oxidation numbers add up to the charge.
  • Not balancing the electrons in half-reactions.

items.q: In 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl, which is the reducing agent?
items.e: Na loses electrons (is oxidised), so it is the reducing agent.

items.q: In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, which is the reducing agent?

items.q: In H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl, which is the oxidising agent?
items.e: Cl₂ gains electrons (is reduced), so it is the oxidising agent; H₂ is the reducing agent.

items.q: What is oxidation?
c: loss of electrons (or an increase in oxidation number)
items.e: OIL RIG: oxidation is loss, reduction is gain.

items.q: What is the best oxidising agent among the halogens?

items.q: Why are blocks of magnesium or zinc attached to ship hulls?
